design_conclusion.accepted: Raise only a currently visible, far, moderate-severity compound target continuously from30 up to36 using obstacle row and image-space sweep.
design_conclusion.formula: target = 30 + 6 * clip((44-y)/12,0,1) * clip((12-sweep)/6,0,1), only for y<44 and6<=sweep<12
design_conclusion.frozen: Near y>=44, extreme sweep>=12, detector miss1--4, noncompound obstacles, clear curves and straights retain their existing targets.

rejected: Global compound30-to36/40: submission12 includes8--12.2px rendered mask gaps and no policy-camera clearance telemetry.
Raise detector-miss latch targets: a miss can mean a close component exceeded detector size bounds rather than true clearance.
Raise extreme sweep>=12: prior hairpin failures were steering-limited even around speed29--30.
Raise straight68, clear-curve40--64 or noncompound47/40: these are already high and are not the localized discontinuity.
Maximum40 far target: an existing normal-obstacle40 upper bound is suggestive but not enough to justify a33-percent compound increase without paired telemetry; maximum36 is the bounded compromise.
limitations: Videos lack physical speed, actions, internal84x84 input, sweep, detector state and source/package receipt binding.
The sweep12 and row44 boundaries are engineering safeguards grounded in existing controller/detector geometry, not video-calibrated physical limits.
HUD target is not physical speed; lateral-demand comparisons are directional only.
Static calculations cannot establish future closed-loop clearance, completion or lap-time improvement.
